title: Large Synoptic Survey Telescope Dark Energy Science Collaboration
extended_summary:
This white paper describes the formation, goals, and organizational structure of the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration (DESC). The central problem is not an educational intervention, but the need to prepare the scientific community to use Large Synoptic Survey Telescope data to study dark energy and related fundamental physics questions with high precision. The paper explains why the LSST Project itself is a facility rather than a scientific collaboration, and why a dedicated collaboration is needed to plan analyses, identify and mitigate systematics, and develop the algorithms, simulations, and computing infrastructure required before data taking begins.

The approach proposed is a coordinated, multi-year research program centered on five dark-energy probes: weak lensing, large-scale structure, Type Ia supernovae, galaxy clusters, and strong gravitational lensing. It also defines cross-cutting work on photometric redshifts, simulations, software, computing, and technical coordination with the LSST system. The paper lays out the initial governance model, working groups, and leadership roles for the DESC, along with the intended three-year work plan.

The context is the international LSST construction and planning effort, with members drawn from universities and laboratories in the United States and France, among other places. The main conclusion is that a large, coordinated collaboration is necessary to fully exploit LSST’s statistical power and to control systematics well enough to make robust dark-energy measurements. The paper argues that this preparatory work will also help the collaboration assess the impact of LSST design choices and survey strategy on future science outcomes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a white paper / collaboration overview for LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration planning, governance, and future analysis priorities, not an empirical study evaluating an educational intervention. It contains no K-12 research design, comparison, or outcome measurement relevant to student learning.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct educational impact evidence because it does not test an intervention or report learner outcomes. Its relevance is conceptual and infrastructural rather than demonstrating measured effects.
